mode_values.report_only: compute every rule and write what it would do to the fan-in and notifier receipts; publish and send exactly as before
mode_values.enforce: publish the reduced incident list and apply the per-source P2 budget; operator activation only

protected.note: Checked before every rule. A protected finding is never dropped, collapsed, demoted, auto-resolved or budgeted.

drop_policy_refusals.note: A diagnoser escalation whose reason is the diagnoser's own policy refusal (it declined to spend a model call, or a remediation run was refused or skipped because the lock was held) is not an incident: the original detector's finding for that lane stays open on its own source.

auto_resolve.note: A run-failure incident tied to a lane closes when that lane's next run (same mode when the incident names one) ends RUN_DONE with exit 0 after the incident was detected. The ledger row is not touched; a dead letter stays in dead_letters for the operator's release.

collapse.note: Diagnoser self-reports collapse to one incident per (lane, failure class); the worst severity wins, the count and the keys are carried as evidence.

demote_low_confidence_p1.note: WS3-35: a low-confidence diagnoser escalation is not 'money or alert path at risk'. P1 -> P2 unless protected.

source_budget.note: Each source may TRIGGER at most this many P2 batch messages per operator day. Over budget, its incidents ride along on a batch another source triggers (shown, never dropped) and the next day's budget sends them. P1-bearing messages no longer count toward the P2 daily cap.
source_budget.recoveries_note: WS3-11: good news must not crowd out bad news. When enforcing, a recovery neither spends nor waits on the P2 cap, and a P2-only recovery leaves at most once per P2 batch window.
